blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, how must the variables in `Point(int a, int b)` relate to the record's components `x` and `y`?

options.text: Named exactly as the components, or it fails to compile
options.says: The page says the variable names in the pattern don't have to match the component names.

options.text: Named freely, though names that match read better
options.says: The page says the names need not match, but matching them improves readability.

options.text: Typed with var, whatever names they are given
options.says: The page suggests var where appropriate, as an option; its own examples also write int.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

questions.stem: Per this page, in which place may a record pattern not be written in Java 21?

options.says: The page's own examples use record patterns with instanceof in Java 21.

options.text: In a `case` label of a switch expression
options.says: The page's own examples use record patterns as case labels in Java 21.

options.text: In the header of an enhanced `for` loop
options.says: The page says record patterns in the enhanced for header were a Java 20 preview, removed in Java 21.

concepts: The variables in a record pattern need not match the component names, and var can infer their types.
A record pattern cannot appear in an enhanced for header in Java 21; that Java 20 preview was removed.
